description: ## Context of Contribution - [ ] Bug Fix - [ ] Refactoring - [x] New Feature - [ ] Others ## Reason for the new feature Hello, I've been using RunCat for four years. I've added a network speed display feature that shows up when you hover the mouse over the system tray icon. This is incredibly helpful for me to check my real-time network speed while watching videos or during downloads/uploads, eliminating the need to install additional software just to monitor my internet speed. ![4e281f68a008fd8dc491a555ed9d1d06](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/504ad5ab-b9b9-40ea-ba72-af446eeb436d) ## Checklist - [x] This PR does not contain commits of multiple contexts. - [x] Code follows proper indentation and naming conventions. - [x] Works correctly in both dark theme and light theme. - [x] Works correctly on any device.

comments.body: The text is garbled. Why is that?
Is there no API that converts numbers into strings with units? The macOS version uses an API called [ByteCountFormatter](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/bytecountformatter).

Is it implemented using only APIs that can be distributed to the Microsoft Store? 
I'm concerned because some PerformanceCounter metrics may be rejected in store review.
Can PerformanceCounters and properties be held within the NetworkRepository, like CPURepository? I want to maintain separation of concerns using the Repository pattern.
It feels odd to include network speed here when memory performance and storage capacity aren't displayed. CPU usage is shown because the cat's speed is based on CPU usage.
This change isn't directly related to network speed information, but rather a bug fix, right? Please do not include this diff in the PR, as I'm currently addressing the issue in #241.
I had a brainstorming session with an AI and it seems okay.
